steps.note: Create the trigger function that copies customer_id into the new bigint column. Takes no lock on orders.
steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$ BEGIN NEW.customer_id_new := NEW.customer_id; RETURN NEW; END $f$;

steps.note: One short transaction: take the table lock with a 300 ms lock_timeout and retry until it is free, so app queries wait 300 ms at most and none time out. Then add a nullable customer_id_new bigint column (a metadata-only change, no rewrite), the sync trigger, and NOT VALID checks that the new column is non-null and equal to customer_id. From here on every new row gets both columns.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOOP BEGIN LOCK TABLE orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 200 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2 + random() * 0.5); END; END LOOP; ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN customer_id_new bigint; CREATE TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF customer_id ON orders FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync(); ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_nn CHECK (customer_id_new IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID, ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_eq CHECK (customer_id_new = customer_id) NOT VALID; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill ids 1..1,000,000 in batches of 50,000, committing after each batch. Only old rows get row locks, and the app never updates rows.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 0 + s * 50000 AND id <= 0 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Vacuum so the next chunk can reuse the space of the dead row versions and the table does not double in size. Does not block reads or writes.
steps.sql: VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 1000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 1000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 2000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 2000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 3000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 3000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 4000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 4000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 5000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 5000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 6000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 6000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 7000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 7000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 8000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 8000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

DO $$ BEGIN FOR s IN 0..19 LOOP UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 9000000 + s * 50000 AND id <= 9000000 + (s + 1) * 50000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL; COMMIT; END LOOP; END $$;
VACUUM orders;

steps.note: Backfill any rows above id 10,000,000 that were inserted before the trigger existed. Rows inserted after it already have the value.
steps.sql: UPDATE orders SET customer_id_new = customer_id WHERE id > 10000000 AND customer_id_new IS NULL;

steps.note: Validate both checks. This takes a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, so app reads and writes keep running. If any row is NULL or differs from customer_id, this fails and stops the plan before anything is dropped.
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_nn; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_eq;

steps.note: Clean up dead rows and collect statistics for the new column. Statistics carry over through the rename, so the /customer query keeps its plan.
steps.sql: VACUUM ANALYZE orders;

steps.note: Swap in one short transaction, with the same 300 ms lock_timeout and retry. SET NOT NULL skips the table scan because the validated check already proves no NULLs. Then drop the trigger and checks, drop the old integer column (its values are proven identical), and rename customer_id_new to customer_id. Catalog changes only, so it takes milliseconds.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE tries int := 0; BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); LOOP BEGIN LOCK TABLE orders IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN tries := tries + 1; IF tries >= 200 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.2 + random() * 0.5); END; END LOOP; ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN customer_id_new SET NOT NULL; DROP TRIGGER orders_customer_id_sync ON orders; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_nn, DROP CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_new_eq; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN customer_id; ALTER TABLE orders RENAME COLUMN customer_id_new TO customer_id; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the trigger function, which is no longer used.
steps.sql: DROP FUNCTION orders_customer_id_sync();

steps.note: Check that orders.customer_id is now bigint NOT NULL.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF (SELECT format_type(atttypid, atttypmod) || '/' || attnotnull FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = 'orders'::regclass AND attname = 'customer_id' AND NOT attisdropped) IS DISTINCT FROM 'bigint/true' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders.customer_id is not bigint NOT NULL'; END IF; END $$;
